title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Notation (from the margin): for an additive category B, B_· denotes chain complexes in degrees ≥ 0, B_* simplicial objects, B^· cochain complexes and B^* cosimplicial objects. ND is the normalization functor and DP the Dold–Puppe inverse.

1. Grothendieck restates the Dold–Kan / Dold–Puppe theorem as an equivalence of categories ND: B_* ⇄ B_· : DP. He requires B to be additive with direct summands, i.e. idempotent-complete (karoubian), and notes that ND and DP are mutually quasi-inverse.
2. Applying this to B° gives the dual equivalence B^* ⇄ B^· between cosimplicial objects and cochain complexes. For B = Ab_k (k-modules) this gives Ab_{k·} ≃ Ab_{k*} and Ab_k^· ≃ Ab_k^*.
3. A small k-linear category K (the universal category built in the preceding pages) carries four structure functors α_·, α_*, α^·, α^* into K_·, K_*, K^·, K^*. The essential images of K^· and K_· under the two DP functors are named K^* and K_*.
4. This yields a square of canonical equivalences: ND/DP horizontally, and vertical contravariant duality functors marked ∨. All of these are compatible with the four α's.
5. A notational convention follows: for an object C of K, write C_·, C_*, C^·, C^* for its images under the α's. Their components are C_n, C_[n], C^n, C^[n], where brackets mark the simplicial or cosimplicial versions as opposed to the complex versions. Arrows marked ∘ are contravariant functors.

Purpose: on the next page Dold–Kan is applied inside the universal k-linear category K. This produces a universal cosimplicial object C^* = DP(C^·), with α_*(C^i) ≅ ∧^{i+1} L_*. The result (Prop. 5) is that for karoubian k-additive B, F ↦ F(C^*) gives Hom_{k-lin}(K, B) ≃ B^*. In other words, K represents cosimplicial objects as well as cochain complexes in karoubian targets: a 'representing-object' or presentation form of Dold–Kan.
errors: No mathematical error on the page. The hypothesis 'additive with direct summands' (idempotent-complete) is exactly what Dold–Kan needs; for merely additive B, DP need not land in the right place and ND need not be essentially surjective.

The labels on the vertical arrows are crossed out and rewritten (∨/∘), and the duality conventions (which arrows are contravariant) are only sketched. The diagram's commutativity is asserted as 'canonical' without verification.

ideas.what: Dold–Kan correspondence stated for additive categories with split idempotents, together with its dual (cosimplicial ↔ cochain) obtained by passing to the opposite category
ideas.modern_name: Dold–Kan correspondence for idempotent-complete additive categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dold (1958), Kan (1958), Dold–Puppe (1961); idempotent-complete version standard (e.g. Lurie HA 1.2.3)
ideas.where_published: Used implicitly in Illusie's Complexe cotangent (Dold–Puppe for simplicial modules); Grothendieck himself discusses Dold–Puppe-type ideas in Pursuing Stacks (abelianization / Dold–Puppe), not in this form

ideas.what: Square of equivalences linking chain complexes, simplicial, cochain and cosimplicial objects in a universal k-linear category K via four structure functors α and duality functors
ideas.modern_name: Dold–Kan as an equivalence of Karoubi envelopes of free linear categories (Z[Δ] vs. the 'd²=0' category); universal (co)simplicial object
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lack–Street, 'Combinatorial categorical equivalences of Dold–Kan type' (2015); also folklore (Lurie HA)

missed.claim: The surrounding pages (this one sets up the notation and diagram) recast Dold–Kan as a representability statement. A universal k-linear category K carries a universal cochain complex C^· and, via DP, a universal cosimplicial object C^*, so that Hom_{k-lin}(K, B) ≃ B^· ≃ B^* for karoubian B. This anticipates the 'Dold–Kan as equivalence of Karoubi envelopes / free linear categories' viewpoint later formalized by Lack–Street and others.
missed.quote: Le théorème de Dold-Puppe peut s'énoncer comme équivalence de catégories (pour les catégories additives avec facteurs directs) ... On a donc un diagramme d'équivalences canoniques
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority only: the categorical-presentation form of Dold–Kan is now standard folklore, but this is an early (c. 1975) explicit formulation by Grothendieck.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is a clean restatement of Dold–Kan for karoubian additive categories, plus its dual and a notation diagram; all of this is standard. The universal-object reformulation (fully visible only on the next page) is an early instance of a viewpoint that is now folklore, so it is mildly interesting historically but not new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: Line 'en particulier' should read Ab_{k·} ≃ Ab_{k*} (subscript dot, chain complexes ↔ simplicial) and Ab_k^· ≃ Ab_k^* (cochain ↔ cosimplicial). The machine transcription gives a superscript dot in the first.

The left margin text near the middle reads approximately: 'k est un anneau ... les essentielles images de K^· et K_· par ces deux foncteurs sont notées K^* et K_*'. The essential images are named K^* and K_*.
The bottom horizontal arrows are labelled ND^· (top) and DP_* (bottom). The vertical arrows carry a crossed-out label replaced by ∨ (duality, contravariant).
The phrase 'Le topos[?] de Dold-Puppe' at the top should be 'Le théorème de Dold-Puppe'.
